text: Ieyasu and Nobunaga were allies for twenty years, from 1562 until Nobunaga's death in 1582.
Ieyasu fought Hideyoshi in 1584, then served him until Hideyoshi's death in 1598, after which he took power.
Itō led the research for the constitution the Emperor granted in 1889, and headed his first cabinet from 1885.
Hideyoshi rose from a peasant background as Nobunaga's retainer. When Nobunaga was killed in 1582, he avenged him at the Battle of Yamazaki and took his place.
Clemenceau bought Monet's paintings by 1884 and stayed a friend Monet confided in about his work.

fr.text: Clemenceau achète des toiles de Monet dès 1884 et reste un ami à qui Monet confie ses doutes sur son œuvre.

text: Monet's collection of Japanese prints at Giverny holds 48 by Hiroshige.
Monet's collection of Japanese prints at Giverny holds 23 by Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa among them.
Rikyū became Nobunaga's tea master in 1579, aged 58.
Rikyū was Hideyoshi's tea master and one of his closest confidants, until Hideyoshi ordered him to take his own life in 1591.
Rodin was commissioned in 1889 to make a monument to Victor Hugo, four years after the writer's death.
Friends from their schooldays in Aix-en-Provence. They drifted apart after Zola's novel L'Œuvre (1886), whose failed painter Cézanne saw himself in.

fr.text: Amis depuis le collège à Aix-en-Provence. Ils s’éloignent après L’Œuvre (1886), le roman de Zola où Cézanne se reconnaît dans le peintre raté.

text: A friend and fellow painter of Manet's, she married his brother Eugène in 1874.

fr.text: Amie de Manet et peintre comme lui, elle épouse son frère Eugène en 1874.

text: As the newly elected president of the French writers' society, Zola strongly supported Rodin for its monument to Balzac.
Zola defended Manet in the press while critics resisted him, and Manet painted his portrait in 1868.
Hugo went into exile under Napoleon III and attacked him in pamphlets such as Napoléon le Petit.
Queen Victoria read Oliver Twist and found it “exceedingly interesting”.
Shakespeare's company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men, played at Elizabeth's court: four performances as early as 1595.
